Citation key chen2021 resolves to Donna Chen, 'Statistical Mediation Analysis in Regression Discontinuity Design for Causal Inference', doctoral dissertation, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, December 2021 (p.19 references); verified against the title page of source/chen2021.pdf (PDF p.1).

Bias negative (source printed p.147: 'When bias was present, the measure of bias was a negative value'); coverage/imbalance (p.150: 'the true parameter value systematically fell above the CIs'); MINT power (p.121: 'All power for MINT is near zero'; p.148: 'never reached the .80 level'); H4 (p.150: 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 has accurate Type I error rates and power above .80, regardless of cutoff score'). All faithful.
Source p.143 indeed says 'Type I error rate and power for all five effects were either within the robustness criteria or reached the ideal range'. Correctly quoted.

findings.location: Table 1 row E4 and caption ('E4 tolerance 0.013 rejection rate (reading error of her figure; her value is within it of zero)')
findings.finding: BLOCKING: the tolerance is the mean reading error 0.01233 rounded UP (build_packet.py: round(mean + 0.0005, 3)), while her unrounded excess is 0.0127 > 0.0123. The 'zero vs nonzero' direction exists only through rounding up; unrounded it is 'same direction'. The packet labels the tolerance kind 'prespecified' while its basis says 'Not set in the plan'; the paper (Section 7.5, p.16) does not disclose either fact.

findings.location: Section 4.3: 'the cutoff 1 point is partly hidden by another series but enters the average, and the two directly read points (0.068 and 0.057) lead to the same conclusion'
findings.finding: BLOCKING (same item): the occluded point (reading error .0187) inflates the tolerance; the two directly read points have mean reading error 0.0092 against an excess of 0.0127, so they do NOT lead to 'within reading error of zero'. Also conflicts with the stated rule that occluded points are not used for verdicts (p.4, p.18).

Rounding tolerances 0.005/0.005/0.01 correctly derived (mean of 2-decimal values; difference of two means); magnitude 'smaller' and directions ('zero vs nonzero' for E1; 'same' for E2, E3) arithmetically correct. Caption carries 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.' POLISH: the MC uncertainty of our 0.04 and 0.33 means is not stated, so the intro's 'point the same way as hers' has no uncertainty qualifier (MC SE of the mean is roughly 0.005-0.02 points).
Nonscalar H4 row: magnitude and direction 'not established', tolerance 'not applicable'. POLISH: effect cells read 'no scalar' rather than 'not established'.

Published 'within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' matches source Table 4.8 (PDF p.102) and p.147; Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% ...; largest |bias| 0.016' matches results/table48_ours.csv and summary.json (0.0155).

Published matches the p.150 sentence including 'Tentative'; Ours 86.3%/89.2%, cutoff similarity and both-zero conservatism match statement_checks.csv summary rows and disagreement_tests.json n5000.both_paths_zero.
